posts.name: 36-world-dinosaur-blood
posts.caption:
Scientists say a 115 million year old dinosaur bone still holds chemical traces of blood 🦖

A team led by Curtin University found tiny cell shaped structures inside leg bones of Aratasaurus, a meat eating dinosaur from Brazil, and detected heme, the oxygen carrying part of hemoglobin, inside them. Not everyone is convinced: molecular paleontologist Mary Schweitzer says the shapes do not match reptile or bird red blood cells. No intact blood survived; the cells were turned to mineral.

Source: Grice et al. (Curtin University, JAMSTEC, Brazilian National Museum, Johns Hopkins University), “Heme signatures in mineralized red blood cells within vascular canals of a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone”, PNAS, 2026.
